label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
which_first: 03, because it is short enough for my five minutes and the four steps on page 5 are the thing I came for.

03.one_line: The cast made me smile and page 5 gave me four steps I can do tomorrow; I only wobbled at 'conductor' and 'hold' until the grey boxes explained them.

10.one_line: Clearer on why it works, and the shop owner examples on page 11 are what made it feel like mine, but the middle pages (5 to 7) read like a log and I skimmed them.

tomorrow: Open a new empty project in the agent tool I used at the building day, write half a page of rules for a small helper that answers the questions customers ask my mum's bakery (what it may change, when it must stop and ask me), write a one-line brief with a Friday deadline, and hand both to the agent.
would_share: yes, with my friend who also finished a first app at the day and keeps saying she does not know what to do next; I would send the four-step page (page 5 of 03, or page 11 of 10).
why_buy: I want a 'do this now' for each stage with real examples like the shop owner, and the pictures that are still to come. It must stay free of code and say what it costs me.

best_page.why: Numbered steps with a shop owner's actual rules and brief written out; this is the page I could copy tomorrow, and it does not feel written for programmers.

worst_page.why: A dashed 'Figure to come' box leads the page, then a fast list of voices (freeze, unfreeze, register) that I could not follow, and it is the page where the book stops being for me.

one_change_before_the_editor_sees_it: On page 9 of the 10-page edition, explain 'freeze' and 'the register' in one plain sentence each, or cut the freeze story down to its lesson; and fill the 'Figure to come' boxes on pages 3, 4, 8 and 9 or hide them, because they look unfinished to someone like me.
notes: Jargon that lost me: 'hold', 'gate', 'debrief', 'register', 'dramatised', 'wake', 'five-step wake'. The small word boxes help but come after I have already met the word. The cover is lovely. The grey 'Where this came from' file paths on the last pages are meaningless to me and made me feel it was for programmers; I would drop them from the reader's copy. Page 6 of 03 has a large empty space. The price line is honest and useful, though a free tool is not named so I do not know which one to open.
